source_text: contrarium ut qui dicit: Vivo non ego iam, vivit vero in me Christus ; dicat etiam: Scio quia non habitat in me, hoc est in carne mea, bonum Apostolum sic ista dixisse, quasi qui se vellet intellegi renitentem, in scorta aliqua manu pestiferae voluptatis abduci
pass_a_gloss: Contrarium so-that/as who he-says: Vivo not ego already, lives but in me Christ; dicat also: knows because not habitat in me, this is in in-flesh my, good apostle thus that dixisse, as-if who himself vellet to-be-understood renitentem, in scorta aliqua manu pestiferae of-pleasure abduci.
pass_b_english: It is contradictory for the person who says, ‘It is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me,’ also to say, ‘I know that good does not dwell in me, that is, in my flesh.’ (Galatians 2:20; Romans 7:18)
You make the apostle say these things as though he meant that, despite his resistance, some hand of deadly pleasure dragged him off to prostitutes.

choices.why: Paul in Julian's citations; keep Apostle not 'Paul' unless Paulus is written.
Keep Julian's good-of-nature vs good-of-will contrast; do not baptize as 'grace'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
